summary: Small 1928 wooden light on a red sandstone cliff at the east end of Île du Havre aux Maisons; the sources disagree on when it went dark (2011 or 2015) and who owns it.

structures.note: 8 m (27 ft) in LighthouseFriends and Rowlett; 8.5 m in the station record

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett). Turn off Chemin Principal (QC-199) onto Chemin de la Pointe Basse.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (per LighthouseFriends and Rowlett; the Corporation says private owner from 2015, non-profit owner from 2025)

events.note: Built at the request of Grégoire Lafrance (LighthouseFriends); the last light established in the Magdalen Islands
Featured on a Canadian postage stamp
Municipal heritage building (immeuble patrimonial), citation dated 17 January 2006
The Corporation says the light went out in 2011; Rowlett and the station record give 2015
Federal heritage status (the Corporation says heritage site)
The Corporation says the lighthouse became private property
Sold to the Société de conservation des Îles-de-la-Madeleine, a non-profit (the Corporation)

notes_for_editor: Read: RPCQ heritage record, Canadian Register statement (French, quoted in French with English paraphrase in the story), Corporation page, LighthouseFriends, Rowlett. Not read: the Parks Canada DFHD page for 14752 (it returned only a script shell). Wikipedia FR was read for leads only and is not cited. It says the land was bought in 2012 by a public figure and reports a 2025 La Presse article; La Presse was not read, and the buyer is not named in the story because the owner is a private person. Conflicts left open: (1) light out in 2011 (Corporation) or 2015 (Rowlett, station record); (2) owner the Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett) or private from 2015 and non-profit from 2025 (Corporation); (3) height 8.3 m (RPCQ, Canadian Register) vs 8 m (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett) vs 8.5 m (station record). The keeper list is the Corporation's, not an official roster; the Marine annual reports in the corpus end in 1924, so 1928 to 1970 keepers are unchecked against an official list. Grégoire Lafrance (the requester and the keeper) is not linked. Whether the tower is open to climbers after the 2025 sale is not known from any source read. The 1903 to 1924 Marine report corpus has no Cap-Alright entry. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story has five chapters (the undated wreck count moved into The place, the hazard the light was built for, since no source dates those wrecks), against the Moderate range of two to four; the editor should decide whether to merge chapters or treat the evidence as Rich.
